summary: AstroHealth is an interactive, gamified health monitoring dashboard designed for long-duration space missions. Combining telecommunications engineering and clinical nursing expertise, our team developed a software system that translates complex biometric telemetry and manual clinical tests into intuitive visual alerts. Addressing the NASA challenge, AstroHealth empowers astronauts to autonomously monitor their physical and mental health without relying on Earth-based ground control. Inspired by survival video games, the tool maps the hazards of spaceflight into visual "survival states" across different anatomical layers, making it easy to identify issues like bone density loss or isolation stress at a glance. By integrating a "Virtual Nurse" clinical algorithm, the tool not only diagnoses but also provides immediate, actionable treatments, ensuring crew survival and well-being.
details:
How it works: AstroHealth divides health monitoring into two branches: automated continuous telemetry (wearables monitoring SpO2, heart rate, EtCO2, stress) and a manual clinical test module (vision, audiometry, bioimpedance) for complex parameters. Data is fed into our "Virtual Nurse" algorithm, which cross-references variables to output actionable treatments.

Benefits & Impact: The primary benefit is immediate visual triage. Long-duration missions bring risks like isolation and hostile environments. Instead of reading raw medical tables, astronauts see a 2D interactive anatomical model that changes color (green/yellow/red) based on the health status of specific layers (surface, bones, muscles, organs). This reduces cognitive load and allows for rapid autonomous response. We also integrated crucial but often overlooked metrics, such as a menstrual cycle tracker for female astronauts, which dynamically alters baseline temperature and stress thresholds.

Creativity: We approached this challenge through gamification. Inspired by survival video games, we transformed NASA's identified spaceflight hazards into visual "Moodles" (altered states). If an astronaut overworks and lacks sleep, a visual anxiety alert triggers, prompting a treatment protocol.

Team Factors: Our design was driven by the unique composition of our team: one clinical nurse and three telecommunications engineers. The telecom engineers designed the data architecture and UI/UX simulation, while the nurse defined the strict decision trees, clinical thresholds, and treatment protocols, ensuring the tool is not just a game, but a scientifically rigorous diagnostic instrument.

Tools & Software: HTML, CSS, JavaScript (for the interactive app logic and SVG manipulation), and Google Sites for deployment.
